title: Rental Yield in Bangalore: Which Areas Give Better Returns in 2026?
seoTitle: Rental Yield in Bangalore: Best Return Areas 2026
body:
A friend buys a 2BHK near Sarjapur Road for 95 lakh, rents it at ₹32,000 a month, and calls it a good deal. On paper, the rental yield in Bangalore terms works out to about 4 percent gross. After maintenance, two months of vacancy, and property tax, the real figure looks rather different. That gap between the number people quote and the number they actually earn is where most investors get their maths wrong. Naverah Assets helps buyers look beyond headline rental yields and understand the actual numbers before making a property decision.

This is worth getting right before you buy, not after. The corridor you pick, the unit size you choose, and the tenant you attract move your return more than any negotiation on the sale price will. With guidance from Naverah Assets, investors can evaluate the location, rental potential, ongoing costs, and overall return more realistically.

What Rental Yield in Bangalore Actually Measures

Yield is annual rent divided by the price you paid, expressed as a percentage. Simple enough, except almost nobody uses the same version of it.

Gross vs Net

Gross yield uses annual rent over purchase price and ignores everything else. Net yield subtracts maintenance charges, property tax, insurance, repairs, brokerage and vacancy, which typically pulls the figure down by 0.7 to 1.2 percentage points. If someone quotes a headline number without saying which one they mean, assume gross.

Why the Denominator Matters

Use your all-in cost, not the agreement value. Stamp duty, registration, Khata transfer, corpus fund and interiors can add 8 to 12 percent to what you actually spent. Leaving them out flatters your property yield Bangalore calculations by a meaningful margin, and that flattery compounds when you compare two properties.

Where the Numbers Sit Today

Bangalore has historically been one of India’s better metros for rental return Bangalore investors can rely on, largely because the tech workforce keeps churning tenants through the same corridors. Gross yields in the city generally land in a low single-digit band, with well-placed compact units at the upper end and large premium apartments at the lower.

The pattern holds across most rental investment areas Bangalore investors track: smaller configurations yield better than larger ones. A 1BHK or compact 2BHK near an employment hub rents at a higher rate per square foot than a 2,000 sq ft unit, because tenant demand is thickest in the budget band where salaried professionals sit.

Ranges are indicative and move with project age, furnishing and micro-location. A unit five minutes from a tech park gate behaves nothing like one twenty minutes away in traffic, even in the same postcode.

Why Central Areas Give a Weaker Rental Yield in Bangalore

Indiranagar and Koramangala command the highest rents in the city, so people assume they deliver the strongest returns. They don’t, usually. Capital values there have risen faster than rents, which mathematically compresses yield. What those areas offer instead is near-zero vacancy and steady capital preservation.

Peripheral corridors invert this. Lower purchase prices and solid tenant demand from nearby offices produce a better rental yield in Bangalore, with more vacancy risk and slower appreciation as the trade-off. Neither is objectively better. It depends on whether you want cash flow or capital growth.

The Costs That Quietly Eat Your Return



Most investors model rent and EMI, then stop, which is how a promising rental yield in Bangalore turns ordinary. The following items are what actually separate projected rental property returns from realised ones.

• Maintenance: typically 3 to 5 rupees per sq ft monthly in gated projects, higher where amenities are extensive.

• Vacancy: budget one to two months a year between tenants, more in oversupplied pockets.

• Brokerage: commonly a month’s rent per tenant change.

• Repairs and repainting: plan for a refresh every two or three tenancies.

• Property tax: annual BBMP payment, small but not zero.

• Income tax: rent is taxable, with a 30 percent standard deduction on net annual value and interest relief on home loans under the applicable provisions.

Work these into your model and a 4 percent gross figure often becomes something closer to 2.8 or 3 percent net. That’s still a reasonable outcome, but it should be the number you plan around.

What Actually Lifts Your Rental Return Bangalore Wide

Small operational decisions move rental yield in Bangalore more than most people expect. A semi-furnished flat with wardrobes, a modular kitchen, lights and fans typically commands a premium over a bare shell, and the fit-out cost usually pays back within two to three years if the tenant profile suits it.

Distance to the nearest tech park entrance matters more than the address, and it shows up directly in property yield Bangalore comparisons. So does floor level, cross ventilation and covered parking, since a car space can add meaningfully to what a tenant will pay. Buildings with reliable power backup and water supply rent faster in the summer months when tanker dependence bites in outer areas.

Tenant profile is the last lever. Corporate leases pay well and stay long but demand higher specification. Sharing tenants and co-living operators push gross rent up while accelerating wear on the unit.

Yield or Appreciation: Pick Your Objective

You rarely get both at full strength, and the strongest rental yield in Bangalore almost never sits where prices are climbing fastest. High-yield pockets tend to be built-out areas near employment with limited scarcity, while high-appreciation pockets are usually emerging corridors where infrastructure is arriving and rental demand hasn’t caught up.

If you’re funding an EMI largely from rent, prioritise yield and low vacancy. If you have surplus income and a seven to ten year horizon, appreciation-led areas like the airport belt may serve you better despite a thinner rental yield in Bangalore during the holding period. Treat this as general information rather than investment advice, and run your specific case past a qualified financial advisor.

Checking Rental Yield in Bangalore Before You Buy

1. Ask three local agents what identical units in that building currently fetch to rent in Bangalore today, not what the developer projects.

2. Check the actual occupancy of the project, since half-empty towers signal weak demand.

3. Verify the rent agreement norms, deposit conventions and notice periods common to that pocket.

4. Confirm A Khata, OC and clean title before you consider any income assumptions.

5. Model twelve months of rent, not eleven, then subtract a vacancy month yourself.

Frequently Asked Questions


1. What is a good rental yield in Bangalore in 2026?

Anything in the low single digits gross is normal for this city, with compact units near tech corridors at the stronger end and large premium apartments weaker. Net of maintenance, vacancy and tax you’ll usually land lower. Compare against your loan rate before deciding whether the deal works.

2. Which unit size gives the best returns?

Compact 2BHK and well-planned 1BHK units near employment hubs generally outperform. They serve the deepest tenant pool, cost less to furnish and refill faster between tenancies. Very large apartments earn more in absolute rupees but a weaker percentage return, and they sit vacant longer when the market softens.

3. Is rent in Bangalore taxable, and how?

Yes. Rental income is added to your total income, with a standard deduction of 30 percent on net annual value plus deduction for home loan interest under applicable rules. Municipal taxes paid are deductible. Tax rules change, so confirm current provisions with a chartered accountant before filing.

4. Should I buy under-construction to improve yield?

Only if you can carry the wait. You earn nothing during construction while paying interest, which drags your effective rental property returns over the full holding period. Ready units start earning immediately. Under-construction can still win if the entry price is materially lower and the developer delivers on time.

Conclusion

The rental yield in Bangalore you eventually earn is decided long before a tenant signs anything. Corridor, unit size, all-in cost and vacancy do most of the work. Compact units near Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Electronic City and the Manyata belt usually give the strongest cash flow, while central addresses trade yield for stability. Build your model on net numbers, include a vacancy month, and verify approvals before you count a single rupee of rent. A conservative model that survives a weak year is worth far more than an optimistic one that needs everything to go right.
